history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Boxanagar is a Buddhist archaeological site at Boxanagar village in the Sonamura subdivision, Sipahijala district, western Tripura, near the Indo-Bangladesh border (~40 km from Agartala; Tripura Tourism says 32 km). Excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India, it holds a massive brick-built stupa of square plan (15.40 x 15.40 m base, over 8 m high) identified with a chaityagriha, a monastery with monk dormitory structures, and sub-structures; the stupa's central chamber yielded large numbers of clay votive stupas and sealings inscribed with religious creeds in Kutila lipi. Local people first took the mound for a Manasa (snake-goddess) temple, but a Buddha idol find confirmed its Buddhist identity. It is a Monument of National Importance (official name 'Ancient Remains, Boxanagar', ASI ref N-TR-2), preserved and managed by the ASI. The district is given as Sipahijala by Wikipedia/Tripura Tourism, though the ASI monument list records it under the older West Tripura district - verify current district.

name: Boxanagar Buddhist Site
town: Boxanagar (CSV town 'Sonamura' is the subdivision, not the site - the ruins are at Boxanagar village, ~40 km from Agartala)
town_description: Boxanagar is a village in the Sonamura subdivision of Sipahijala district, western Tripura, on the fringes of the Indo-Bangladesh border (~40 km from Agartala). It is chiefly known for the ASI-excavated Buddhist ruins - stupa, chaityagriha and monastery - which draw weekend visitors and are being developed for border-area tourism.

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala (~40 km)
travel.road: Sonamura subdivision, ~32-40 km from Agartala; visitors note the connecting road from the highway to the stupa is in poor condition
